info.title: Crossfeed API
info.description: Act for one network: its roster, launches, and inbox. Authenticate with one of the network's API keys, made by an owner in its settings, as `Authorization: Bearer cf_live_…`. Nothing here approves an insertion order or a reply: only a member does, in the app. Long work, such as an import, answers 202 with the resource's current status; poll the resource until it settles. Examples use made-up shows and figures.

post.description: Send the roster file as the body: a CSV with a `name` column and optional `downloads`, `status`, and `description` columns, or plain text with one show name per line, at most 50 shows and 5 MB. It answers 202 at once with the new shows pending; poll the roster until it settles. Over a roster that has shows, it needs `replace=true`: shows already on it keep their matches, comps, and exclusions, the figures the file brings change, and only new shows are looked up.

post.description: Send the pitches as the body: one email as `message/rfc822` (an .eml file), an mbox export as `application/mbox`, plain text with a line of three dashes between pitches as `text/plain` (a pitch's first lines may give its `From:` and `Subject:`), or JSON pitches, at most 50 pitches and 5 MB. Of each email, only its sender, subject, and text are kept, never its attachments or other headers, and only its work's title and type reach Qloo. An email with no text, or over 10,000 characters, is skipped and named. It answers 202 at once with the pitches reading; poll the inbox until it's done. Reading the pitches counts as one of the network's model runs. Over an inbox that has pitches, it needs `replace=true`: they go, with the last pitch run's lists and replies.

post.description: Rank the inbox's pitched works against a roster show matched in Qloo, and against its best past guests' works too, then draft a reply to every pitch. Only each work's title and type reach Qloo, never a guest's name or a sender. It answers 202 at once with the run running; poll it until it's done or waiting on a question. It counts as one of the network's model runs, and a new run ends one left waiting.

post.description: Rank the network's roster, as it stands now, by fit with the launch's listeners in Qloo, then plan its promos to a draft insertion order priced at the network's CPM. With no body, the run plans the launch as it stands; a name or comps plan it anew. It answers 202 at once with the run running; poll it until it's done or waiting on a question. It counts as one of the network's model runs: past the network's daily model runs, it stops at once, saying why. A new run ends one left waiting.

post.description: Answer the question the run is waiting on, by its ID, with the fields its kind takes: `choice` or `text` for a `choice` question; `choice` (one of its options) or `text` (the name Qloo lists the launch under) for `launch`; `slots` or `dollars` for `budget`; `exclude`, from its options, for `exclusions`; `comps` or `text` for `comps`; and `picks` for `confirm_comps`. Relay the question to the person planning the launch and answer with their words. The run resumes, answering 202; poll it again.
